paper_metadata.title: Kimi k1.5: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with LLMs
paper_metadata.abstract: Language model pretraining with next token prediction has proved effective for scaling compute but is limited to the amount of available training data. Scaling reinforcement learning (RL) unlocks a new axis for the continued improvement of artificial intelligence, with the promise that large language models (LLMs) can scale their training data by learning to explore with rewards. However, prior published work has not produced competitive results. In light of this, we report on the training practice of Kimi k1.5, our latest multi-modal LLM trained with RL, including its RL training techniques, multi-modal data recipes, and infrastructure optimization. Long context scaling and improved policy optimization methods are key ingredients of our approach, which establishes a simplistic, effective RL framework without relying on more complex techniques such as Monte Carlo tree search, value functions, and process reward models. Notably, our system achieves state-of-the-art reasoning performance across multiple benchmarks and modalities -- e.g., 77.5 on AIME, 96.2 on MATH 500, 94-th percentile on Codeforces, 74.9 on MathVista -- matching OpenAI's o1. Moreover, we present effective long2short methods that use long-CoT techniques to improve short-CoT models, yielding state-of-the-art short-CoT reasoning results -- e.g., 60.8 on AIME, 94.6 on MATH500, 47.3 on LiveCodeBench -- outperforming existing short-CoT models such as GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 3.5 by a large margin (up to +550%).

extraction_data.innovation: Scaling RL context window to 128k using partial rollouts; variant of online mirror descent for policy optimization; long2short method using length penalty and model merging; simplistic RL framework without MCTS, value functions, or process reward models.
extraction_data.pretraining_corpus: Diverse, high-quality multimodal corpus covering English, Chinese, Code, Mathematics Reasoning, and Knowledge; includes Captioning, Image-text Interleaving, OCR, Knowledge, and QA datasets
extraction_data.application: Math, coding, vision, general reasoning, long-context reasoning
extraction_data.research_problem: Scaling reinforcement learning with LLMs to unlock a new axis for continued improvement beyond static datasets.
extraction_data.finetuning_data: High-quality long-CoT warmup dataset (text and image inputs); RL prompt set spanning STEM, coding, general reasoning, text-only and image-text QA
extraction_data.extension: Partial rollouts establish a fixed output token budget, capping rollout trajectory length; unfinished segments are saved to a replay buffer and continued in the next iteration, eliminating repeated rollouts and reducing computational overhead.
extraction_data.paper_title: Kimi k1.5: Scaling Reinforcement Learning with LLMs
extraction_data.training_pipeline: Pretraining -> vanilla SFT -> long-CoT SFT -> RL
extraction_data.synthetic_data_generation_method: Automated test case generation for coding using CYaRon library and base Kimi K1.5
extraction_data.reward_mechanism: Verifiable ground truth answers; critic model provides feedback to evaluate progress and identify errors; pass rate used as proxy for prompt difficulty
extraction_data.training_environment_scale: Kubernetes-based code sandbox supporting multi-stage assessments and consistent evaluation across programming languages
extraction_data.benchmark_result: AIME 2024: 77.5; MATH 500: 96.2; Codeforces: 94th percentile; LiveCodeBench v5: 47.3; MathVista: 74.9; MMMU: 62.5; MMLU: 87.4; IF-Eval: 87.2; CLUEWSC: 76; C-Eval: 76.7
extraction_data.post_training_infrastructure: Large-scale RL training system with Trainer Workers, Rollout Workers, Master node, Replay Buffer, and Reward Models
